content:
Guiding Claude (Opus 5.5), I've had Claude create a Lean4 proof that formalizes Umans and Lenhart's (paper, thesis) polynomial time algorithm to find Hamiltonian cycles in 2D solid grid graphs.

The repo can be found a zzyzek/SolidGridGraphHamiltonianCycle2D-Lean. The project compiles with the three axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

I was mostly concerned with the invariants of the algorithm, namely that alternating strips exist, that they make progress etc. and so I wasn't focused on getting tight runtime bounds. The runtime bound is $O(|V|^{12})$ and is almost surely not tight. Claude informs me (and is also documented in the README) that the runtime performance is done through a step-counting monad.

I'm not sure if others will find it useful but I thought I would announce it here in case anyone was interested. I am, otherwise, a complete beginner regarding my ability to program in Lean.

Any constructive criticism is welcome.
This topic was moved here from #computer science > Umans and Lenhart's Ham Cycle in Solid Grid Graphs by Michael Rothgang.
